fatal_errors: Thermal or compositional treatments intended to induce SRO would also change phase fractions, residual stress, grain size, interface coherency, and chemistry, so the proposed comparison does not isolate SRO.
The selected outcomes—hcp fraction, pileups, and work-hardening behavior—do not directly establish creep resistance or distinguish rate-controlling creep mechanisms under a constant-load hold.
No cited evidence directly demonstrates controllable interface-specific SRO or SRO-controlled creep in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses sustained deformation in nanoscale HEA multilayers and is independently testable, but it does not reconstruct the target study. It replaces modulation-period-controlled coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary interfaces with an unreported SRO treatment and omits the 8/16/32/80 nm comparison, room-temperature nanoindentation conditions, stress-exponent analysis, and the distinctive minimum in creep rate and stress exponent at 16 nm. Its SRO-to-slip-resistance and reduced-hcp arguments have general support in HEAs and nanocrystalline alloys, but the evidence does not validate interface-localized SRO, increased interfacial stacking-fault energy, or creep control in this FCC/BCC coating system. A stronger experiment would directly quantify SRO while holding interface coherency and microstructure fixed, then compare creep displacement, steady-state strain rate, and stress exponent across multiple loads or loading rates.
